nodes.name: Ni-MOF Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: A DMF solution of 1,4-H2BDC (0.032g in 4.5mL) and a DMF solution of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.029g in 4.5mL) were mixed. This solution and 3mL H2O were transferred to a 20mL Teflon vessel and stirred into a homogeneous solution. The sealed vessel was placed in a stainless-steel autoclave and heated in a 150°C oven for 4h. After cooling to room temperature, the product was collected by centrifugation and washed at least 3 times with H2O and EtOH before drying at 60°C overnight.

nodes.name: Ni/NiO-PGC10-1-400 Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: 60 mg of Ni-MOF was weighed into a porcelain boat. They were annealed in a tube furnace heated to the fixed temperature (400°C) with 10% H2/N2 flow for 1 h. After the heating was stopped and cooled to room temperature, the pyrolysis product was exposed in the air.

nodes.name: Ni/NiO-PGC5-2-400 Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: 60 mg Ni-MOF was pyrolyzed in a tube furnace at 400°C for 2h in a 5% H2/N2 flow. The sample was collected after cooling to ambient temperature in the 5% H2/N2 flow.

nodes.name: NiO-PC Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: 60 mg Ni-MOF placed into a tube furnace at 400°C for 8h in a flow of N2. The sample was collected after cooling to ambient temperature in the N2 atmosphere.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show stacked lamellar nanosheets morphology retained after pyrolysis for Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM (Fig. S5 in the ESM) and TEM (Fig. 1(a)) images showed that the overall morphology of the stacked lamellar nanosheets of Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400} was retained after pyrolysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Ni/NiO heterojunction NPs with size 8-20 nm well dispersed in carbon matrix for Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In each nanosheet, TEM analysis revealed that the Ni/NiO heterojunction NPs with a size of 8-20 nm were well dispersed in the carbon matrix (Figs. 1(b) and 1(c)).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with d-spacings of 0.204 nm (Ni(111)), 0.178 nm (Ni(002)), 0.241 nm (NiO(111)), 0.209 nm (NiO(200)) and graphene shells ~2 nm thick covering Ni/NiO NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Higher magnification HRTEM image (Fig. 1(f)) disclosed clear lattice fringes with a d-spacing of 0.204 and 0.178 nm, corresponding to the (111) and (002) planes of nickel, and a d-spacing of 0.241 and 0.209 nm, corresponding to the (111) and (200) planes of NiO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM with EDX mapping shows uniform distribution of C, Ni, O elements throughout Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM coupled with EDX mapping revealed the almost overlapping images of the three elements of Ni, O, and C (Fig. 1(e)), illustrating that C, Ni, and O are evenly distributed throughout the Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400} composites.

properties.description: Multi-panel TEM/SEM image with elemental mapping

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows polycrystalline Ni/NiO with diffraction rings for Ni(111), (002), (022) and NiO(111), (220) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1(g), the five unambiguous diffraction rings are well assigned to the crystal planes of (111), (002), and (022) of Ni as well as the (111) and (220) planes of NiO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD shows Ni(0) peaks at 44.6°(111), 51.9°(002), 76.5°(022) and NiO peak at 37.2°(111) for Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400}, consistent with SAED.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1(h) shows the PXRD patterns of Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400}, with reflection peaks at 44.6°, 51.9°, and 76.5° corresponding to the (111), (002), and (022) planes of Ni(0) and the peak at 37.2° corresponding to the (111) plane of NiO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows I_D/I_G = 1.18 indicating high graphitization degree for Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400} with NiO phonon peaks confirming NiO presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The increase in the ratio of I_D/I_G from 1.18 (Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400}) to 1.31 (Ni/NiO-PGC_{5-2-400}) suggests the decreased graphitization of carbon in Ni/NiO-PGC_{5-2-400}.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption-desorption shows specific surface areas of 157.82 m²/g (Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400}), 126.93 m²/g (Ni/NiO-PGC_{5-2-400}), 122.97 m²/g (NiO-PC) with micro/mesoporous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: They exhibited large specific surface areas of 157.82, 126.93, and 122.97 m²·g^{-1}, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows Ni⁰ at 852.3 eV, NiO at 853.6/855.6 eV; Ni(0) proportion 24.73% in Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400}, 13.18% in Ni/NiO-PGC_{5-2-400}; C 1s and O 1s confirm graphitization degree.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2(a), Ni 2p_{3/2} exhibits a peak at 852.3 and two peaks at 853.6 and 855.6 eV, which could be ascribed to Ni^0 and NiO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX shows C 66.3 at%, Ni 21.1 at%, O 12.6 at% in Ni/NiO-PGC_{10-1-400} with Ni/O ratio >1 confirming Ni/NiO coexistence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX spectra showed that the contents of C, Ni, and O in Ni/NiO-PGC 10-1-400 are 66.3 at.%, 21.1 at.% and 12.6 at.% respectively (Fig. S4 in the ESM).
